```{r}
# Load required packages for data manipulation, date handling, tables, and plotting
library(tidyverse)
library(lubridate)
library(knitr)
library(scales)

# Purpose: Reads and cleans a single year's raw EPA air quality CSV file into daily averages.
# Arguments:
#   file_path - character string giving the path to the yearly CSV file.
#   o3_units  - character string specifying output units for Ozone ("ppm" or "ppb"); defaults to "ppm".
# Returns:
#   A clean tibble with one row per Date and columns CO, PM25, and O3.
process_air_quality <- function(file_path, o3_units = "ppm") {
  df <- read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE) # Import raw CSV data
  df <- df %>% distinct() # Remove exact duplicate rows before aggregation or modification of values
  df <- df %>% mutate(Date = mdy(Date) %>% as.Date()) # Parse Date strings into standard Date objects
  
  # Locate pollutant concentration columns dynamically by matching column name patterns
  co_col <- grep("CO Concentration", names(df), value = TRUE)
  pm_col <- grep("PM2.5 Concentration", names(df), value = TRUE)
  o3_col <- grep("Ozone Concentration", names(df), value = TRUE)
  
  # Replace negative measurement error values with zeroes across all pollutant columns
  for (col in c(co_col, pm_col, o3_col)) {
    df[[col]] <- ifelse(df[[col]] < 0, 0, df[[col]])
  }
  
  # Convert Ozone from ppm to ppb if requested (1 ppm = 1,000 ppb)
  if (o3_units == "ppb") {
    df[[o3_col]] <- df[[o3_col]] * 1000
  }
  
  # Aggregate multiple readings on the same day into daily averages and rename cleanly
  df %>%
    group_by(Date) %>%
    summarise(
      CO = mean(!!sym(co_col), na.rm = TRUE),
      PM25 = mean(!!sym(pm_col), na.rm = TRUE),
      O3 = mean(!!sym(o3_col), na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}

# Process each yearly dataset
aq_2018 <- process_air_quality("AQ_2018.csv") %>% mutate(Year = 2018)
aq_2019 <- process_air_quality("AQ_2019.csv") %>% mutate(Year = 2019)
aq_2020 <- process_air_quality("AQ_2020.csv") %>% mutate(Year = 2020)

# Combine all processed years into a single data frame
all_aq_data <- bind_rows(aq_2018, aq_2019, aq_2020)
```

```{r}
# Build a wide summary table of min and max daily concentrations for a given year, formatted to 3 decimals
gen_table <- function(df, yr) {
  sub <- df %>% filter(Year == yr)
  
  tibble(
    `Pollutant (Units)` = c("CO (ppm)", "PM2.5 (ug/m3 LC)", "O3 (ppm)"),
    Minimum = sprintf("%.3f", c(
      min(sub$CO, na.rm = TRUE),
      min(sub$PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
      min(sub$O3, na.rm = TRUE)
    )),
    Maximum = sprintf("%.3f", c(
      max(sub$CO, na.rm = TRUE),
      max(sub$PM25, na.rm = TRUE),
      max(sub$O3, na.rm = TRUE)
    ))
  )
}

# Render separate summary tables for 2018, 2019, and 2020
# Left align text columns, right align numerical columns
kable(
  gen_table(all_aq_data, 2018),
  caption = "2018 Minimum and Maximum Daily Pollutant Concentrations",
  align = c("l", "r", "r")
)

kable(
  gen_table(all_aq_data, 2019),
  caption = "2019 Minimum and Maximum Daily Pollutant Concentrations",
  align = c("l", "r", "r")
)

kable(
  gen_table(all_aq_data, 2020),
  caption = "2020 Minimum and Maximum Daily Pollutant Concentrations (Jan–Apr)",
  align = c("l", "r", "r")
)
```

```{r}
# Pool daily measurements by calendar month across all available years to compute means and 95% CIs
monthly_pooled <- all_aq_data %>%
  mutate(Month = month(Date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE)) %>%
  group_by(Month) %>%
  summarise(
    CO_mean = mean(CO, na.rm = TRUE), CO_sd = sd(CO, na.rm = TRUE), CO_n = sum(!is.na(CO)),
    O3_mean = mean(O3, na.rm = TRUE), O3_sd = sd(O3, na.rm = TRUE), O3_n = sum(!is.na(O3))
  ) %>%
  mutate(CO_ci = 1.96 * (CO_sd / sqrt(CO_n)), O3_ci = 1.96 * (O3_sd / sqrt(O3_n)))

scale_factor <- 10 # Scale O3 by 10 on the primary axis so both seasonal curves are visually legible alongside a secondary axis

# Create plot for Monthly Average CO and Ozone from 2018-2020
ggplot(monthly_pooled, aes(x = Month)) +
  geom_point(aes(y = CO_mean, color = "CO"), size = 2.5) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = CO_mean - CO_ci, ymax = CO_mean + CO_ci, color = "CO"), width = 0.2) +
  geom_point(aes(y = O3_mean * scale_factor, color = "O3 (x10)"), size = 2.5) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = (O3_mean - O3_ci) * scale_factor, ymax = (O3_mean + O3_ci) * scale_factor, color = "O3 (x10)"), width = 0.2) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = "CO Mean (ppm)", sec.axis = sec_axis(~ . / scale_factor, name = "Ozone Mean (ppm)")) +
  scale_color_manual(name = "Pollutant", values = c("CO" = "#D55E00", "O3 (x10)" = "#0072B2")) +
  labs(title = "Monthly Average CO and Ozone (2018-2020)", x = "Month") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```
```{r}
# Create a plot for daily PM2.5 distributions across abbreviated months grouped by year using boxplots
all_aq_data %>%
  mutate(Month = month(Date, label = TRUE, abbr = TRUE), Year = as.factor(Year)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Month, y = PM25, fill = Year)) +
  geom_boxplot(alpha = 0.7, outlier.size = 1) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2") +
  labs(title = "Daily PM2.5 Concentrations by Month and Year", x = "Month", y = "PM2.5 (ug/m3 LC)", fill = "Year") +
  theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Textual description:
Ozone ($O_3$) shows a clear seasonal pattern peaking in warmer months (around June) and reaching its lowest levels in late autumn and winter (November–December), while carbon monoxide (CO) trends in the opposite direction with higher means in cooler months (December–January) and lower levels in late spring and summer. Daily $PM_{2.5}$ exhibits moderate month-to-month variation and occasional high spikes, notably standing out in 2020 with a maximum concentration of 31.200 $\mu\text{g/m}^3$ compared to 20.400 $\mu\text{g/m}^3$ in 2018 and 21.300 $\mu\text{g/m}^3$ in 2019. Because 2020 data only cover January through April, estimates for May through December reflect two years of data (2018–2019) and carry wider uncertainty than January–April.
